chapter: First jobs and finding his sound
title: Wanting the best: Hawkins's example and the Mercedes
summary: He patterned his life on Hawkins and Ben Webster and wanted a Mercedes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: You know I was thinking of something when you told the story about Coleman Looking at this automobile for sale in a car showroom. I remember Cedar Walton said the other day that he'd never known what a Mercedes Benz car was until he saw that you had one...when he first knew you.

Yeah, well, you know I've always wanted the best in life that I could, you know, because you know I learned from Coleman...because when you see Ben Webster, he was always sharp. They always had the best saxophones in the world and they always sounded so beautiful. So I patterned my life like that, I looked for...so I says, "This guy might like a Buick, but I
wanted a Mercedes because I rode in one one time and it was just like sitting in your livin' room." I says, "Look, that's what I want." Hahahaha.
